newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil, small firms agree to scrap tax-cut bills.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, small firms agree to scrap tax-cut bills.

text.p: The Brazilian government and representatives of small businesses agreed to scrap two controversial bills that would have exempted small companies from tax and instead negotiate a new law, a deputy said.
The bills, which were due for a vote in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday, would have slashed about $4 billion from tax revenues, according to government calculations.

Dep. Joao Coser, from the Workers Party and a representative of the Parliamenary Front for Small Firms, said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso had agreed that the new legislation should be through Congress by the end of the year.

Coser did not give any details of what the new bill might look like. Newspapers have said the government is offering to set up a single tax bracket for small companies of 10 percent and reduce their employer contributions.
The scrapped bills were the creation of Sen. Jose Sarney, a former Brazilian president and current president of Congress, who has been critical of the government's economic policies.
